content.text: The minimum monthly fee exists, so I checked whether an exit right neutralizes it.

input.quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits \"A\" and \"B\" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale: Section 5(a) does impose monthly minimums on us for Hosting and Support Services, but the commitment is bounded and exitable, so it sits at (or slightly better than) the fallback position. The term is a single one-year period renewing in one-year increments (§ 13), so no multi-year commitment is locked in, and either party can prevent renewal on thirty days' notice. More importantly, § 14 gives us a unilateral termination right for convenience: on written notice, TrueLink continues services only "until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate," which is effectively a 30-day exit that stops the minimums accruing. There is no shortfall payment, take-or-pay make-whole, liquidated damages or penalty for failing to reach the minimum, and no volume cap on our usage — we simply pay the monthly minimum for months in which the Agreement is on foot, which is a true-up rather than a penalty. Two sub-points worth noting commercially rather than redlining here: the minimum amounts are left blank ($____) and must be filled with figures at or below our expected run-rate before signature, and § 6 carves the "minimum monthly fees" out of our documentation and charge-dispute rights (the cross-reference to "Section 4" appears to be a mis-numbered reference to the Compensation section). Neither defeats the fallback on this rule.
